title: Build an ATS-Friendly Resume and Practice DSA
description: Create a one-page ATS-optimized resume and solve 10 Python DSA problems on LeetCode
objective: Students will create a one-page ATS-friendly resume with quantified project descriptions, test it against a job description using an ATS scanner, and solve 10 DSA problems on LeetCode to prepare for technical interviews

steps.title: Write Your Resume Content
steps.instructions:
Before formatting, write the raw content for your resume in a text file.

Create a file called `resume-draft.txt` and fill in these sections:

**1. Header:**
```
YOUR FULL NAME
Python Full-Stack Developer
City, India | your.email@example.com | +91-XXXXXXXXXX
GitHub: github.com/username | LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/profile
```

**2. Skills (one line, comma-separated):**
```
Python, FastAPI, Django, PostgreSQL, SQLAlchemy, HTML, CSS, JavaScript,
HTMX, Docker, Git, GitHub Actions, LangChain, REST API, SQL, Linux
```

**3. Projects (most impressive first):**
For each project, write 3-4 bullet points starting with action verbs.
Include at least ONE number/metric in each project.

Example:
```
SmartAttend — Student Attendance Management System        Jul 2026
FastAPI | PostgreSQL | HTMX | LangChain | GitHub Actions
- Built a full-stack web app for managing attendance of 200+ students
  at TechPath Institute, reducing manual paperwork by 80%
- Developed 8 REST API endpoints with JWT authentication, Swagger docs,
  and pagination handling up to 10,000 records
- Integrated AI chatbot using LangChain RAG that answers natural language
  queries about attendance data with 95% accuracy
- Set up CI/CD with GitHub Actions (lint, test, deploy) achieving 85%
  code coverage across 20+ automated tests
Live: smartattend.example.com | Code: github.com/username/smartattend
```

Write descriptions for at least 3 projects. Every bullet must:
- Start with a verb: Built, Developed, Implemented, Deployed, Designed, Created, Integrated
- Include at least one number (users, endpoints, percentage, time saved)

steps.title: Format Your Resume as a Clean PDF
steps.instructions:
Use one of these free tools to format your resume:

**Option A: FlowCV (Recommended for beginners)**
1. Go to https://flowcv.com
2. Create a free account
3. Choose a simple, single-column template (no graphics, no icons)
4. Enter your content from the draft
5. Download as PDF

**Option B: Google Docs**
1. Open Google Docs
2. Use a simple template or start blank
3. Set margins to 0.5 inches
4. Use a clean font: Arial, Calibri, or Helvetica (size 10-11)
5. Use bold for section headings
6. Download as PDF

**Option C: Overleaf (LaTeX — advanced)**
1. Go to https://www.overleaf.com
2. Search for "Jake's Resume" template
3. Fill in your content
4. Compile and download PDF

**ATS Rules to Follow:**
- [ ] Single page only (one side)
- [ ] No tables or multi-column layouts
- [ ] No images, icons, or graphics
- [ ] No headers or footers (ATS ignores them)
- [ ] Standard section headings: Skills, Projects, Education
- [ ] Save as PDF (not Word)
- [ ] File name: `YourName-Resume-2026.pdf`

**Section Order for Freshers:**
1. Name + Contact
2. Skills
3. Projects (most impressive first)
4. Education
5. Certifications (optional)

steps.title: Test Your Resume with an ATS Scanner
steps.instructions:
Now test if your resume will pass ATS filters.

**Step 1: Find a sample job description**
Go to https://www.naukri.com or https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/ and search for "Python Developer fresher" or "Backend Developer."

Copy a job description that matches your skills.

**Step 2: Test with an ATS scanner**

Go to https://resumeworded.com/score (free tier):
1. Upload your resume PDF
2. Paste the job description
3. Click "Score My Resume"
4. Read the feedback

Alternatively, use https://www.jobscan.co (free scan):
1. Upload resume
2. Paste job description
3. View the match score

**Step 3: Improve based on feedback**

Common fixes:
- **Missing keywords**: Add technologies mentioned in the JD to your Skills section
- **Weak bullet points**: Add numbers and metrics
- **Too long**: Cut to exactly one page
- **Wrong format**: Remove tables, columns, or graphics

**Target: Score at least 60% match on the ATS scanner.**

If you score below 60%, revise and re-test until you pass.

Save your final resume as `YourName-Resume-2026.pdf`.

steps.title: Solve 10 DSA Problems on LeetCode
steps.instructions:
Create a LeetCode account at https://leetcode.com if you do not have one.

Solve these 10 problems in Python. They are commonly asked in fresher interviews:

**Arrays:**
1. **Two Sum** — https://leetcode.com/problems/two-sum/ (Easy)
2. **Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock** — https://leetcode.com/problems/best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock/ (Easy)
3. **Contains Duplicate** — https://leetcode.com/problems/contains-duplicate/ (Easy)

**Strings:**
4. **Valid Palindrome** — https://leetcode.com/problems/valid-palindrome/ (Easy)
5. **Valid Anagram** — https://leetcode.com/problems/valid-anagram/ (Easy)
6. **Longest Common Prefix** — https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-common-prefix/ (Easy)

**Hashmaps:**
7. **Roman to Integer** — https://leetcode.com/problems/roman-to-integer/ (Easy)
8. **Majority Element** — https://leetcode.com/problems/majority-element/ (Easy)

**Other:**
9. **Valid Parentheses** — https://leetcode.com/problems/valid-parentheses/ (Easy)
10. **FizzBuzz** — https://leetcode.com/problems/fizz-buzz/ (Easy)

**For each problem:**
1. Read the problem carefully
2. Think about the approach for 5 minutes before coding
3. Write your solution in Python
4. Submit and make sure all test cases pass
5. If stuck for more than 15 minutes, look at the discussion tab for hints

**Time target:** Solve each problem in under 15 minutes.

After solving all 10, take a screenshot of your LeetCode profile showing 10+ problems solved.

steps.title: Prepare Your Interview Cheat Sheet
steps.instructions:
Create a file called `interview-prep.md` with answers to the 10 most common interview questions.

Write your answers in your own words (not copy-pasted). Keep each answer under 5 sentences.

```markdown
# Interview Preparation — Quick Reference

## HR Questions

### 1. Tell me about yourself
[Write a 2-minute pitch: your background, what you learned at TechPath,
your capstone project, what you are looking for]

### 2. Why should we hire you?
[Mention: your projects prove you can build real products,
you know the full stack, you have deployed a live app]

### 3. What is your greatest strength?
[Name one strength + give a specific example from your capstone]

## Technical Questions

### 4. What is REST API?
[Your answer — mention: HTTP methods, resources, status codes,
stateless, JSON responses]

### 5. What is the difference between list and tuple in Python?
[Your answer — mention: mutability, performance, use cases]

### 6. What are decorators in Python?
[Your answer — mention: functions that wrap other functions,
@syntax, use cases like @app.get in FastAPI]

### 7. What is ORM? Why use it?
[Your answer — mention: Object-Relational Mapping, write Python
instead of SQL, SQLAlchemy example]

### 8. Explain the difference between SQL JOIN types
[Your answer — INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL — with simple examples]

### 9. What is JWT authentication?
[Your answer — JSON Web Token, stateless, header.payload.signature,
used in your capstone]

### 10. What was the hardest bug in your project and how did you fix it?
[Your real answer — describe a specific bug using the STAR method:
Situation, Task, Action, Result]
```

Fill in ALL 10 answers with your own words.

Practice reading your answers out loud — you should be able to answer each one smoothly in under 2 minutes.

Congratulations — you now have:
- A polished resume ready for job applications
- 10 DSA problems solved on LeetCode
- An interview cheat sheet for quick revision

You are ready to apply for jobs.

expected_output: A one-page ATS-friendly resume in PDF format that scores at least 60% on an ATS scanner, 10 solved LeetCode problems visible on the student's profile, and a completed interview preparation document with answers to 10 common questions
